# PLAN — iteration 5
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible and has 1.387 ns register-to-register WNS. Recent candidates passed implementation checks but were rejected because their register-to-register slack was lower. The current seed is a transposed eight-tap FIR with a registered output; its default coefficients are symmetric, but the independently overridable parameters mean that symmetry cannot be assumed for every configuration.

## Hypothesis
Use elaboration-time coefficient-equality checks to pair symmetric tap samples when their coefficients match, reducing the default implementation from eight multipliers to four and forming a balanced sum that may improve routed setup slack.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the `x_d` and `acc1`–`acc7` transposed accumulation structure with an eight-sample delay line and a registered sum of its taps, preserving the current output cycle alignment and synchronous reset behavior. For each symmetric tap pair, use a signed pre-add and one multiplication only when that pair’s coefficient parameters are equal; otherwise retain the exact two independent products, so all supported parameter overrides preserve their behavior. Sum the resulting 32-bit products modulo 32 bits with a balanced tree, retain `// @latency 1`, and evaluate against the incumbent’s 1.387 ns register-to-register WNS with all fixed verification and routed-report gates.
